newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes mixed, new contract low in March.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes mixed, new contract low in March.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with March finishing lower after setting a new contract low of $3.56-1/2 per bushel in early dealings, traders said.
"Stops were hit at the (previous) contract low of $3.57," a trader said. The previous low of $3.57 was set Friday and that level Monday and Tuesday evolved into a significant chart support area.

"We made new lows but held above the $3.57 level at the close," a trader said. "There was pretty decent support at fifty-seven. But tomorrow morning if we take that out there may be some sell signals."
Skepticism about a significant pickup in U.S. wheat exports despite a spate of light volume business overnight weighed on the March contract, they said.
Taiwan overnight bought 61,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, a Korean flour mill bought 15,400 tonnes and the Philippines invited tenders to buy 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.
Also, Pakistan set a tender for February 16 to buy 360,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian wheat.
Wheat closed 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 higher, with March down 3-3/4 at $3.57-3/4.
Chartists early Tuesday cited first support in the March contract at $3.58 per bushel and second support at $3.52.

Also, "spreaders are pressuring the March," a trader said. Low-volume bear spreading of the July/March and May/March was noted, traders said, with support in the July coming from mounting concerns about the condition of U.S. winter wheat.
"The decline in condition ratings helped new crop wheat," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
State agricultural statistics services Monday said the condition of the Oklahoma and Kansas hard red winter wheat crop declined slightly during January.
Also there were some rumblings that some U.S. soft red winter wheat may have been damaged by harsh winter weather.

But agronomists said on Tuesday that concern over recent temperature swings in key U.S. soft red winter wheat growing areas may have caused heaving and hurt fledgling crops, appeared to be largely unfounded.
"We have had some of the right kind of weather for heaving but not enough of it to be a problem right now," said James Beuerlein, professor of agronomy at Ohio State University.
Technicians said the four- and 20-day moving averages remained bearish for CBOT wheat futures.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for March closed at 22.4 percent. Technical traders generally consider an RSI of 30 or less as a barometer of an oversold market.
Speculators, including funds, were key sellers while commercials were small-lot buyers.
Merrill Lynch Futures sold 2.5 million bushels of March and Dean Witter sold 1.5 million March, traders said.
ADM Investor Services bought one half million bushels of March, Cargill Inc bought one half million May and Prudential Securities bought 1.5 million March and bought 2.5 million May, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 12,000 contracts, below the 16,735 traded Monday.
In wheat options, Dean Witter sold 500 July $3.40 calls at 16-3/4 to 17 cents and Refco Inc bought 500 May $3.90 calls at 3-1/2 to 3-3/8 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, below the 9,791 traded Monday.
